candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XLIX.10. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be'. Ephrem reads this as the most explicit messianic prophecy in Genesis: Shiloh = the one to whom (Hebrew shelo = 'his') everything belongs / the one who is sent. Tewahedo Christology preserves the Shiloh-as-Christ identification load-bearingly: the Tewahedo qǝddase explicitly cites Gen 49:10 as proof-text for Christ's Judahic descent and universal lordship ('unto him shall the gathering of the people be').
